content.text: (b) Drive in the bushing from the inside of the block with a suitable tool.
The oil hole should be positioned toward the crankshaft side.
(c) Make sure the front mark of the bushing is positioned toward the front of the block.
There are two ways of oil seal replacement.
1. IF TIMING BELT CASE IS REMOVED FROM CYLINDER BLOCK (Replacement of front oil seal and pump drive oil seal)

content.description: Illustration showing SST tool removing and installing oil seal with timing belt case removed

items: (a) Using a screwdriver, remove the oil seal.
(b) Apply MP grease to the oil seal lip.
(c) Using SST, install the new oil seal.

content.text: 2. IF REAR OIL SEAL RETAINER IS REMOVED FROM CYLINDER BLOCK (Replacement of rear oil seal)

content.description: Illustration showing SST tool removing and installing rear oil seal

items: (a) Using a screwdriver, remove the oil seal.
(b) Apply MP grease to the oil seal lip.
(c) Using SST, install the new oil seal.

content.text: 3. IF TIMING BELT CASE IS INSTALLED ON CYLINDER BLOCK (Replacement of front oil seal)

content.description: Illustration showing SST tool removing front oil seal with timing belt case installed

items: (a) Using SST, remove the front oil seal.

content.description: Illustration showing SST tools installing front oil seal with timing belt case installed

items: (b) Apply MP grease to the oil seal lip.
(c) Using SST, install the new oil seal.
